Operational values are reversible coaching choices inside the envelope, never physiological thresholds, injury-prevention rules, readiness scores, finish-time promises or individual-response predictions.
Steps advance only on executed comparable work without an adverse signal; nothing progresses from elapsed calendar time alone; completed history and official plan state stay immutable.

One progression dimension per session type per week; EARNED may release a step the cadence would otherwise hold or skip a consolidation hold, but never adds more than one step on any dimension in a week, and is unavailable in WALK_JOG, RESTART and RETURN modes.

Every step requires executed comparable sessions without an adverse signal in the gating week; quality/strides activation, block-boundary set increases and ladder steps count executed weeks, never calendar weeks.

Single-run ceiling (operational.run.singleRunCeiling): no planned run other than the race exceeds the longest completed run of the preceding 30 days (completed-work ledger, the intake-reported longest current run while within 30 days of intake, a valid return demonstration) by more than one stepMinutes; walk/jog ladder sessions and walks follow the ladder, whose start never holds more jogging per session than the longest current run (D42); with nothing completed in the window the reviewed entry (return.entryRunMinutes) is the ceiling in every week, not only the first.

When the 30-day reference run is under 50 minutes, the 5-minute step exceeds 10% of it; the step stays response-gated, is disclosed, and is never combined with another single-session increase in the same week. A long-run step that the long-run share cap holds is not a single-session increase: that week the easy step and the quality step proceed under their own gates and cadence, and if either steps the long-run target waits where it was prescribed. In such a week the stepped easy run may equal the long run prescribed that week, never exceed it. A long run held at the single-run ceiling is still a step beyond the 30-day reference (D50, resolved in round 10).

Strength ADVANCE requires logged target repetitions and minimum logged RIR >= prescribed RIR - 1; EARNED requires minimum logged RIR >= prescribed RIR + 2 on two comparable exposures outside consolidation; a known-load or bodyweight repetition or load step requires a logged set for that exercise in the gating week; missing logs or unknown logged RIR hold the dose without regression; a logged load above the plan never becomes the reference unless that exposure met the ADVANCE criterion (D44).

longRunShareOfWeeklyMinutesMax limits long-run growth in weeks with at least three running sessions; the cap holds the long run and never shortens it below the typical easy run or the last build week's long run; consolidation, taper and return reductions are separate rules.
Transition magnitudes (restart step and switch point, walk/jog exit dose, consolidation reduction, post-event redevelopment) are declared in the policy, not hard-coded.
Repeated adverse responses (two comparable within 14 days at the current dose after any regression) regress one step; a single adverse response holds.

A run dimension or exercise with no executed session in the reviewed week holds: it never counts as an executed week, never advances a walk/jog step, never unlocks quality or strides and never converts a walk. In a conditional projection a week with no planned session of a dimension likewise never counts as executed for it (D46).

After an exercise is re-established by effort, its prescribed set count, including any block-boundary set, returns at most one set per executed week without a phase reduction, never two at once, whatever the state's mode at the re-establishment (D53: resolved in round 12 for a known-load state, still open for a from-log state; required before FREEZE-2).

Return-entry and return-step exposures never count toward a block-boundary set increase: a development block with any such exposure of the exercise earns no set, including the block in progress at the break. After the return steps the set count comes back at most one set per executed week without a phase reduction, up to the ceiling (the last set count executed before the break outside a phase reduction), with phase reductions on top; it goes above the ceiling only through a later development block with no return-step exposure (operational.return.strengthReturnSets; D49, shared with R6-NONCLINICAL-RETURN).

With no easy run planned in a week (every easy day a walk), the executed long run gates the development-week count and the walk-to-run conversion; a converted walk becomes an easy run at run.minimumSessionMinutes that then progresses like the others (R12). In a conditional projection, restart and return sessions of any role gate on EASY, as in reviews (R13).

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. A week that receives no gating review keeps the projection's assumption that it was executed and logged (establishment, progression, block credit, achieved peaks and the strength resume clock); that path is outside this approval and must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference (R18).

envelope.claim: A planned, response-gated trajectory with one progression dimension per session type per step, small absolute steps and periodic consolidation weeks is a defensible recreational progression model.
limits: no ten-percent or other universal injury rule is claimed
planned future doses are conditional proposals, not predictions
no progression from elapsed calendar alone

Operational values are reversible coaching choices inside the envelope, never physiological thresholds, injury-prevention rules, readiness scores, finish-time promises or individual-response predictions.
Steps advance only on executed comparable work without an adverse signal; nothing progresses from elapsed calendar time alone; completed history and official plan state stay immutable.

Interruption reasons are structured; any illness, injury, pain or clinical category, or a whole-word clinical-lexicon match in free text, routes CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED regardless of nonclinical or clinicalReason flags; an ambiguous or missing reason is ASK; the same rule applies to the intake pause and the legacy path.
Current eligibility must be assessed on or after the interruption end date.
SHORT (<= shortMaxDays): resume the last executed doses; the first quality slot runs easy; the next step waits for executed sessions.

MODERATE (<= moderateMaxDays): run entry from a current demonstration (modality RUN, easy/long/recovery-easy family, completed, conversational effort, compatible response, ordinary and next-day function, observed after the interruption began and within currentDemonstrationMaxAgeDays) or the reviewed 15-minute entry; at most moderateStepsToPrior conditional steps to the prior executed dose, each within the single-run ceiling of R6-PLANNED-PROGRESSION.

Strength return: every strength exposure of the return-entry week, including exercises first set up in it, is strengthEntrySets set(s) at RIR >= strengthEntryMinimumRir with the prior load only as a ceiling. Return step 2 is max(1, min(ceiling - 1, strengthEntrySets + 1)) sets at RIR 3, the ceiling being the last set count executed before the break outside a return step and outside a phase reduction (else the known count, else the normal count). Afterwards the count comes back at most one set per executed week without a phase reduction, up to the ceiling (a phase-reduced step 2 is followed by the step-2 count itself), and goes above it only through a later development block with no return-step exposure. Consolidation, specific, taper, race-week and post-event reductions apply on top, in the return steps too. Return-entry and return-step exposures never count toward a block-boundary set increase. During the return steps a logged load is capped at the current return reference (the load before the break until an entry log is adopted, then the adopted entry load) and asked about; the prior KNOWN load is prescribed only after a post-interruption logged entry load supports it, otherwise FROM_LOG from the entry log (D49; operational.return.strengthReturnSets, returnLoadCap).

LONG (> moderateMaxDays): restart class for running, with the achieved run peaks and the longest continuous run cleared so that taper, race-week, race-day and next-block doses and the race-day statement come only from runs executed after the restart (operational.return.restartRunHistory); strength re-establishes by effort; no prior-load KNOWN prescription until a post-interruption log exists.
EARNED is unavailable during RETURN/RESTART; surplus counts only observations after the return started.
No universal percentage rollback; historical maxima are ceilings, not current proof.

A nonclinical return requires a structured nonclinical reason category (legacy R5 contract: clinicalReason=false) and current eligibility assessed on or after the interruption end with every clinical flag false; free text can only add CLINICAL or ASK outcomes.

Interruption facts out of range or contradicting each other (days outside 1-3650 or not whole, unreal dates, start after end, dates after the review, days and dates disagreeing by more than one day) are asked, never resolved to the least conservative class; a clinical flag that means yes in any form routes to a human, one that is neither yes nor no is asked.
A run demonstration shorter than run.minimumSessionMinutes is not used as a demonstration.

Additions to the free-text screen (clinical terms, phrases, the damage-verb plus body-part rule) may only add CLINICAL or ASK outcomes; body parts alone stay ASK; a damage statement whose every damage verb is locally negated is ASK, never NONCLINICAL; a negation elsewhere in the clause never hides an affirmed damage statement.

A clinical eligibility flag that means yes in any form routes CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED in the intake, the review and the legacy path, as does a clinical status in any letter case; any other non-boolean flag leaves eligibility unassessed (ASK), never clearance and never assumed illness.
The round-8 lexical additions (R11) only add CLINICAL or ASK outcomes; 'Paternity leave' and 'Funeral and grief' stay nonclinical; conservative false positives are owned-gap residuals.

The return ends for every exercise: an exercise not used during the return steps carries no return step once the exercises in use complete theirs, and rotation resumes on its cadence afterwards. In use means prescribed in the week, executed or not: a missed in-use exposure keeps its exercise at its step and the return open, and a week without strength exposure ends nothing (D51, resolved in round 10; dossier Q2).

An exercise that reappears after a return without having been performed during it is established by effort when it was never performed (including one first prescribed in a session dated inside the pause) and re-established by effort when it was last performed more than return.moderateMaxDays earlier, counted from its last executed exposure (D52, resolved in round 11).

A never-performed exercise prescribed during a return gets the return-entry dose while any exercise in use is at the entry step and, once performed, joins the return at that step; if every exercise in use has passed the entry step, it is established by effort (at most 2 sets at RIR >= 3) and then progresses as a new exercise. The second case is to be declared in the next policy revision (R17).

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. A week that receives no gating review keeps the projection's assumption that it was executed and logged (establishment, progression, block credit, achieved peaks and the strength resume clock); that path is outside this approval and must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference (R18).

envelope.claim: After a known nonclinical interruption with current ordinary function, re-entry starts from current evidence (a current demonstration or the R4 entry) and returns to the prior tolerated dose in conditional steps, scaled by interruption length.
limits: no universal percentage rollback
historical maxima are a ceiling, not current proof
illness, pain, injury or unknown cause never receive this recipe

Steps advance only on executed comparable work without an adverse signal; nothing progresses from elapsed calendar time alone; completed history and official plan state stay immutable.

Supported events are 10K and half-marathon only; one taper week plus the race week, progressive: taper-week easy runs within taperWeekRunVolumeRange and the long run within taperWeekLongRunRange of the executed peak; taper quality total work minutes within taperQualityWorkRange; race-week easy runs within raceWeekRunVolumeRange; the policy states these are per-session fractions.

Frequency is maintained; intensity is maintained only through work already executed in build/specific weeks; a race-effort touch at the policy dose >= raceWeekTouchMinDaysBeforeRace days before the race requires R6-RUN-QUALITY and an executed comparable quality session; shakeout strides require executed strides; otherwise easy.

Strength stays at a reduced dose: taper sets about taperStrengthSetFraction of the preceding dose at RIR >= 3; race week one session of raceWeekStrengthSets at RIR >= raceWeekStrengthMinimumRir no later than raceWeekStrengthMinDaysBeforeRace days before the race; no new exercise, load increase or rotation.

Post-event: no running before postEventFirstRunMinDaysAfterRace days; runs optional and easy within postEventEasyMinutes; one light strength session; redevelopment (NEXT_BLOCK) requires an eligibility and function assessment dated after the race; redevelopment fractions are declared in the policy.
The legacy path uses the athlete's event kind and only policy-declared fractions.
No finish-time, readiness or peak-performance claim.

Event proximity counts days to the race (raceWindowDays 6; 7 taper days per taper week before the window): race-window sessions have no long run and no quality, an optional shakeout the day before, at most one race-effort touch on the run day closest to the race that is >= raceWeekTouchMinDaysBeforeRace days out, and short easy runs; taper-day sessions take taper doses whichever calendar week they fall in; post-race sessions follow the post-event rules by days since the race; a race date marked unavailable is asked about.
In WALK_JOG or RESTART mode, taper-day, race-window and post-event run sessions are reductions or holds of the achieved session of that mode, never a continuous run the mode has not reached (D43a).

Race day is a completion prescription at conversational effort with walk breaks (jog bouts no longer than achieved), without strides and without an instruction to press, when the race-week mode is WALK_JOG, RESTART or RETURN, when the athlete was in WALK_JOG or RESTART mode in any week of the program before the race (D47), or for a half marathon whose achieved long run is below raceDayCompletion.halfMarathonAchievedLongRunBelowMinutes; race-day warm-up strides and shakeout strides for any athlete only after executed strides (D43b-c, R9).

Whenever race day is a completion, the program or the proposal carries the non-blocking negotiation, recomputed from the race-week state of every proposal (added, replaced or removed), stating the longest continuous run executed by race week (never 0 when such a run was counted; a restart after a long interruption starts the count again), why race day is a completion, and both options (keep the event with walk breaks; a later or shorter event) (D43d, D47).
In taper weeks and at the start of the next block the long run is never shorter than that week's easy run (R10).
Walk/jog and restart steps do not advance on taper, race-window or post-event days; the next block resumes the walk/jog ladder one step back.
No exemption from the history-based completion applies unless it is declared and reviewed (D47c).

An exercise re-established by effort in a taper, race-window or post-event session takes that session's reduced strength dose: never more sets than the phase dose the exercise would otherwise have that day and never fewer reps in reserve than the phase minimum; the load stays effort-guided under its earlier ceiling (D54, required before FREEZE-2).

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. A week that receives no gating review keeps the projection's assumption that it was executed and logged (establishment, progression, block credit, achieved peaks and the strength resume clock); that path is outside this approval and must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference (R18).

envelope.claim: For recreational 10K and half-marathon events, a progressive volume reduction over the final one to two weeks while maintaining session frequency and a short intensity touch, with strength kept at a reduced dose and stopped in the final days, followed by an easy nonclinical post-event week, is a defensible event transition.
limits: no finish-time guarantee or readiness claim
no new intensity, overload or new exercise in the taper
no fixed universal recovery day count after the race; function and eligibility are checked

Severity is ordinal only: compare Pareto first, then by leximax of the sorted severity multiset (worst first); counts or sums of costs are not used.

Any run, easy included, within sameSessionGapHours before MODERATE/HEAVY lower-body work carries a strength-axis cost when strength has a development role; no tie-break depends on candidate identifier strings; equal-harm opposing trade-offs under a JOINT lead are ASKed.

Quality-run-first may be the default for an equal-standing athlete only when the alternative places MODERATE/HEAVY lower-body work within nextDayGapHours before the key run; the choice is disclosed as a reversible population-based default, the athlete may choose otherwise, and repeated comparable athlete evidence may override it; for accustomed lifters the asymmetry is weaker and must be disclosed as such.

Unknown arrangement-level response is admissible only when current whole-week tolerance covers the same task set and frequency, the candidate's worst H0 severity is <= LOW, and it introduces no same-day pairing absent from the athlete's reported routine; otherwise it needs arrangement evidence or ASK; adverse arrangement evidence excludes it.
The trace names the decisive comparison (for example LOWEST_WORST_CASE_JOINT_HARM) whenever non-identical candidates were compared.
No universal spacing minimum; the gap bins rank options and never forbid a feasible arrangement by themselves.

Cold start: same-day pairings arising from the athlete's own chosen days and shifts are admissible and ranked; when the selected arrangement carries a MODERATE or higher H0 cost the program discloses it and offers the shift or day change as a negotiation option.

Near an event, arrangements follow days to the race: no strength in the last raceWeekStrengthMinDaysBeforeRace days; at most one short light session (raceWeekStrengthSets sets, main lifts, RIR >= raceWeekStrengthMinimumRir) on the strength day furthest from the race inside the race window; strength on taper days takes the taper dose.

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. A week that receives no gating review keeps the projection's assumption that it was executed and logged (establishment, progression, block credit, achieved peaks and the strength resume clock); that path is outside this approval and must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference (R18).

envelope.claim: Residual-fatigue interactions between sessions differ by direction and gap: heavy lower-body resistance work within roughly the preceding day can impair a key run more than a controlled run impairs next-day strength; same-session order matters most; upper-body work interacts little with running.
limits: ordinal classes only, never summed into a score
individual athlete evidence may override the population ordering
self-reported tolerated arrangements stay admissible
An arrangement whose own combined response is unknown stays admissible with disclosed uncertainty when current whole-week tolerance covers the same tasks; adverse arrangement evidence excludes it

pooling.arrangementPreferenceQuery: sessionType + phaseClass + doseKey (quality family, ladder and step of the current quality session); no query without a current quality dose

learning.missingGate: A run dimension or exercise with no executed session in the reviewed week has no gate and holds; in a conditional projection a run dimension advances only when the week plans a session of it (SSCTR D46), and restart and return sessions of any role gate on EASY there, as in reviews (SSCTR R13). Such a dimension never counts as an executed week, never unlocks quality or strides and never converts a walk. A week with no easy run planned (every easy day a walk) uses the executed long run for the development-week count and the walk conversion instead; the first converted walk becomes an easy run at run.minimumSessionMinutes that then progresses like the others (SSCTR R12).
learning.conflicts: A report that conflicts with another for the same session (same event id with different facts, different physical facts or responses, or one wearable activity bound to two sessions) stays in the completed-work record, flagged, and is quarantined: the session is CONFLICTED for gating and the facts count for neither capacity nor learning until a correction resolves them. A report dated before the activity it reports is rejected.
learning.consentScope: Without learning consent the athlete model stays empty and no athlete-specific pattern (learned rearrangement or learned preference) changes the plan; gating on the plan’s own completed-work record does not depend on learning consent.

tests.name: Adaptation: executed as planned → KEEP; the official plan and completed work are never changed
Adaptation: a missed long run is zero work, no debt; only that step repeats (H0–H3 traced)
Adaptation: mid-week reviews never gate next week as if future sessions were missed
Adaptation: a missed key run in the specific phase moves only to a later chosen day without added interference
Adaptation: repeated adverse responses regress one step, then hysteresis holds
Adaptation: repeated easier executions earn one step, never two; walk/jog never earns (SSCTR D11/D12)
Adaptation: local fatigue removes only optional local work; systemic convergence removes remaining hard work
Adaptation: equipment loss substitutes by movement intent, establishes unfamiliar work and converts no load
Adaptation: a substitution persists through later weekly reviews (SSCTR D27)
Adaptation: a schedule change re-arranges future weeks on the new chosen days only
Adaptation: an event date change re-plans phases; a date outside the horizon asks for a new program
Adaptation: nonclinical return is staged from current evidence; clinical or unknown cause is never given a recipe
Adaptation: clinical flags route to a human and stay sticky through generic recovered labels
Adaptation: invalid chronology, missing timezone or stale eligibility hold or ask rather than guess
Adaptation: duplicates, conflicts and future facts never double-count or change a past decision
Adaptation: a goal or date change with nothing new asks for it; the same goal again keeps the plan
Adaptation: a selected KEEP is always an admissible counterfactual, including weeks with logged loads that change nothing
Adaptation: a learned rearrangement applies and records the week’s gates, so hysteresis sees its regression
Adaptation: interruption reasons are screened by category and whole words; illness never gets a nonclinical recipe (SSCTR D08)
Adaptation: return eligibility must postdate the interruption; only a conversational easy run counts as a demonstration (SSCTR C6, D09)
Adaptation: after the race, redevelopment waits for an eligibility check dated on or after race day (SSCTR D04)
Simulation: 4-, 8-, 12- and 16-week trajectories run end to end with every invariant
Simulation: strong adherence keeps the plan; supported events reach race week and post-event
Simulation: irregular adherence holds affected steps without debt; the missed key run is moved once
Simulation: repeated surplus earns, repeated adverse regresses, single signals hold, conflicts stay uncertain
Simulation: interruptions, schedule change, substitution and fatigue are handled with the smallest valid change
Simulation: no official-plan effects and no completed-work rewrites anywhere
